# Pull Requests, Issues and Replies

Full rules, evidence and examples: `common/writing/pr-issue.md`.

- PR-01 must: Make the PR title the commit subject: Conventional Commits, lowercase, imperative, with the `; fix #N` suffix when it applies.
  Good: title `feat: add retry option; fix #12`.
  Bad: title `Feat/retry-option`.
- PR-02 must: Leave the PR body empty or one line: a `BREAKING CHANGE:` line, a `fix #N`, or one sentence of why; do not restate the diff.
  Good: body `fix #12`.
  Bad: a body that lists every changed file and restates the diff.
- PR-03 lean: In a longer PR body open with the change in one lowercase sentence, then a short list of what changed, then blockers as a task list with links.
- PR-04 prefer: Do not add a PR template; keep PR bodies free-form, with the commit subject as title and a body only when needed.
- PR-05 lean: In a PR to a project that is not the owner's, explain the use case in 2 to 3 sentences, say what is minimal and untouched, thank the maintainer in one line, and follow the target's template.
- PR-06 prefer: Title an issue as a Title Case noun phrase naming the capability or problem, without a Conventional Commits prefix.
- PR-07 prefer: In an issue state the current situation, the wanted solution and the constraint in short paragraphs; use bullets for options, links to docs or code, and `- [x]` tasks; use no template headings.
- PR-08 prefer: In a bug report to someone else give versions, the exact setup, the observed behavior, what you ruled out, then logs in a code block; start a feature request with the use case and the risk it removes.
- PR-09 must: Reply to strangers in a friendly, direct tone: thank once, say what is known, say what is needed, give the next step; apologize plainly and once for a real own error or delay.
  Good: "thanks for the report. reproduced on 2.3; can you attach the debug log? then the fix is next."
  Bad: "Hopefully this should fix it!!!"
- PR-10 prefer: Start every sentence lowercase in replies and issue bodies, the first one included; titles use Title Case. Use standard case in greetings and text to maintainers of other projects; keep code, versions and product names exact.
- PR-11 must: Ask for missing facts as a short list, each with a purpose: version, debug logs, a minimal program, output of the failing command; ask the reporter to redact secrets.
  Good: "to narrow this down, please send: the version, the debug log (redact tokens), and the output of the failing command."
  Bad: "Doesn't work for me either, any news?" or "Please provide more info."
- PR-12 prefer: If the cause is upstream, say so with the reason, ask the reporter to try upstream directly, open an issue there and link it, and keep the local issue open until it is fixed.
- PR-13 prefer: Decline in this order: thank, say it is not planned or you are reluctant, give the technical reason in a few lines, offer what you can do (docs, an alternative, accepting a fitting PR); no blame.
- PR-14 prefer: Announce a fix with the exact version in backticks; for a beta ask the reporter to test it; close after confirmation or with `closing due to being stale`.
- PR-15 lean: Thank a contributor once and briefly; ask for a rebase, CLA or failing checks plainly; if you redo the change, link the commit and close.
- PR-16 prefer: Explain behavior as a short numbered flow or a list of options with the favored one and why; link the code line or doc section instead of paraphrasing it.
- PR-18 must: Add no attribution to PR text: no "Generated with" line and no AI trailer, whatever the tool's default adds (COMMIT-17).
  Good: body `fix #12` and nothing after it.
  Bad: a body ending in a "Generated with ..." line or a `Co-Authored-By:` AI trailer.
